name: The Elgin Mount Pandim, Pelling
summary: A hotel run by the Elgin group on the ridge just below Pemayangtse Monastery, with lawns that face Kangchenjunga across the Rangeet valley. The quietest premium address in West Sikkim, a short walk from Pemayangtse and Rabdentse.
body: The Elgin Mount Pandim sits on the Pemayangtse ridge at a little over 2,000 m, a few minutes on foot from the gate of Pemayangtse Monastery and about 2 km from the Pelling market. The Elgin group also runs hotels in Darjeeling and Gangtok, and the house style is the same here: old-fashioned service, a fireplace lounge, gardens and set-menu dinners. On a clear morning between October and April the lawn looks straight at Kangchenjunga and Kabru.

We book it for couples and older travellers who want calm rather than nightlife. Upper Pelling's cafes are a short drive away, but most guests stay in for dinner. Because the hotel is below the main Pelling ridge, you walk to Pemayangtse before the day visitors arrive and to the Rabdentse ruins by the forest path. Rates change sharply by season, so treat our band as a guide and check current status before you travel.
why: A five-minute walk to Pemayangtse Monastery
Kangchenjunga view from the lawns on clear mornings
Quiet location away from Upper Pelling traffic

faqs.q: How far is The Elgin Mount Pandim from Pelling market?
faqs.a: It is about 2 km below Upper Pelling on the Pemayangtse road, roughly 10 minutes by car. Pemayangtse Monastery is a five-minute walk from the hotel gate and the Rabdentse ruins about 20–30 minutes on foot. Most guests keep a car for the day for Khecheopalri, Yuksom and the waterfalls, which are 1–2 hours away on hill roads.

faqs.q: Can you see Kangchenjunga from The Elgin Mount Pandim?
faqs.a: Yes, on clear days. The view from the lawns runs across the Rangeet valley to Kangchenjunga, Kabru and Pandim. The best odds are between mid-October and March, at sunrise. From June to September cloud usually hides the range for days at a time, so we never promise a view in the monsoon.

faqs.q: Is The Elgin Mount Pandim good for families with children?
faqs.a: It suits families who want a calm base with gardens to walk in, but it is not a resort with activities or a pool. Children who like monasteries and short walks enjoy it. Families wanting a livelier place close to cafes may prefer a hotel in Upper Pelling. Ask us about connecting rooms and extra beds, which vary by room type.

name: The Chumbi Mountain Retreat and Spa
summary: A large resort in Pelling from the group behind The Chumbi Residency in Gangtok, with a spa, several dining options and rooms that face Kangchenjunga. A good premium choice for families and couples who want resort facilities close to the Pelling sights.
body: The Chumbi Mountain Retreat and Spa is one of the bigger hotels in Pelling, run by the same family group as The Chumbi Residency in Gangtok. It sits close to the Pelling town area, so Sanga Choeling, the Chenrezig statue and Skywalk, Pemayangtse and Rabdentse are all a short drive. Rooms on the mountain side look towards Kangchenjunga when the sky is clear.

We use it for families and couples who want a spa, room service and space after long drives on the Gangtok–Pelling road. It is busier than The Elgin Mount Pandim and better for groups. Prices swing a lot between peak weeks (October, Durga Puja, Christmas, May) and the monsoon, so we quote live rates and add the ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee collected at check-in. Check current status before you travel.
why: Spa and resort facilities after long hill drives
Short drive to Pemayangtse, Rabdentse and the Skywalk
Larger property that handles family groups well

faqs.q: Is The Chumbi Mountain Retreat in Upper Pelling?
faqs.a: It is in the Pelling town area, within a short drive of Upper Pelling's market, the helipad viewpoint and the road to the Chenrezig statue and Skywalk. Pemayangtse and Rabdentse are about 10 minutes away by car. Ask us for a mountain-facing room if the Kangchenjunga view matters to you, as not every room faces the range.

faqs.q: Does The Chumbi Mountain Retreat have a spa?
faqs.a: Yes, the hotel has a spa offering massages and other treatments, which is a big part of its appeal after the 5–6 hour drive from Gangtok or Siliguri. Treatments are paid separately and are best booked on arrival. Timings and menus change, so ask at the desk or let us check before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does a night at The Chumbi Mountain Retreat cost?
faqs.a: Indicatively ₹9,000–18,000 a room a night, depending on room type, season and meal plan. Peak weeks in October, late December and May cost the most; July and August are cheapest. Rates usually include breakfast. The ₹50 per person Sikkim tourist fee is collected at check-in. We quote live prices when you enquire.

name: Norbu Ghang Retreat and Spa
summary: A well-known Pelling resort with wide Kangchenjunga views, a café and a hot stone bath spa. Our usual comfort-tier pick in Pelling when the view comes first and budgets sit below the premium hotels.
body: Norbu Ghang is one of the longer-established hotel names in Sikkim, and its Pelling retreat is built for the view: rooms and terraces face north to Kangchenjunga, Kabru and Pandim. It has its own café serving bakes and snacks, and a spa known for the dotho, the Sikkimese hot stone bath in which river stones heated in a fire are dropped into a wooden tub of water.

We pick it for couples and families on our comfort journeys who want good rooms without paying premium rates. The Pelling sights are a short drive, and the hotel can arrange sightseeing cars. As with every Pelling hotel, the view depends on weather: October to March is clearest. Rates are a band, not a quote, and the ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee is extra. Check current status before you travel.
why: Mountain-facing rooms and terraces
Hot stone bath spa and an in-house café
Comfort-tier prices below the premium hotels

faqs.q: What is the hot stone bath at Norbu Ghang?
faqs.a: It is a version of the Sikkimese and Tibetan dotho bath: river stones are heated in a fire and lowered into a wooden tub of water, warming it slowly. People use it to ease stiffness after long drives and treks. It is paid separately at the spa. Ask at the desk for timings, and avoid it if you have heart or blood pressure concerns.

faqs.q: Is Norbu Ghang good for a honeymoon in Pelling?
faqs.a: Yes, it is one of our regular honeymoon picks in Pelling at the comfort level. Ask for a mountain-facing room, plan sunrise from the terrace between October and March, and pair it with a morning at Pemayangtse and the Rabdentse ruins. For a quieter and more expensive stay, The Elgin Mount Pandim is the step up.

faqs.q: How do I reach Norbu Ghang from Bagdogra?
faqs.a: Bagdogra to Pelling is about 145 km and 5–6 hours by private car via Melli, Jorethang and Legship. A reserved car costs indicatively ₹5,500–7,500 one way. Shared jeeps from Siliguri go to Gyalshing, from where a local taxi covers the last 10 km. In the monsoon slides can add hours, so check current status before you travel.

name: Summit Newa Regency, Pelling
summary: A Summit Hotels property on the Pelling–Pemayangtse side of town with a spa and mountain-facing rooms. A solid comfort-tier base a few minutes by car from Pemayangtse and Sanga Choeling.
body: Summit Newa Regency belongs to Summit Hotels, a Sikkim and Darjeeling group, and sits a few minutes' drive from Pemayangtse Monastery and Sanga Choeling. It has a spa, free wi-fi and a tour desk, and its mountain-facing rooms look towards Kangchenjunga on clear days.

We use it when Norbu Ghang is full or when a family wants a modern hotel with lifts and predictable service. It works well as a two-night base for Pelling sightseeing plus a day trip to Khecheopalri and Yuksom. Rates are a band, include breakfast on most plans and rise in October, late December and May. Check current status before you travel.
why: Short drive to Pemayangtse and Sanga Choeling
Spa and modern rooms with a tour desk
Reliable comfort-tier option in busy weeks

faqs.q: How far is Summit Newa Regency from Pemayangtse Monastery?
faqs.a: About a three-minute drive, and Sanga Choeling is about six minutes by car to the start of the climb. The Rabdentse ruins are 10 minutes away. This makes it a practical base for an early monastery visit before day-trippers arrive from Gangtok, Ravangla and Darjeeling. Upper Pelling's cafes are also a short drive.

faqs.q: Do Summit Newa Regency rooms have a Kangchenjunga view?
faqs.a: Mountain-facing rooms do, on clear days. Ask for one specifically when booking, because not every room faces north. The clearest months are mid-October to March, and early morning is best. From June to September cloud usually covers the range, which is when rates are lowest.

faqs.q: Is Summit Newa Regency suitable for senior travellers?
faqs.a: Yes. It is a modern hotel with lifts, short walks to the car and a restaurant on site, which suits older travellers better than older hillside buildings with many steps. Pelling sits at about 2,150 m, so take the first evening slowly and drink water. Tell us about mobility needs and we will request a suitable floor.

name: Yuksum Residency
summary: One of the better hotels in Yuksom, with a terrace and garden, used by families on the Pelling–Yuksom circuit and by trekkers resting before or after the Goecha La trail. A short walk from the bazaar, Norbugang and Kathok Lake.
body: Yuksom has few proper hotels, and Yuksum Residency is one of the more comfortable. It has a terrace and garden, rooms that are warm enough in winter with extra blankets, and a restaurant that feeds trekkers and families. The bazaar, Kathok Lake and the Norbugang coronation site are within walking distance, and the trail to Dubdi Monastery starts on the edge of the village.

We use it for value journeys that spend a night in Yuksom rather than rushing back to Pelling, and for trekkers who want one comfortable night after eight or nine days on the trail. Power cuts happen in Yuksom; ask about backup. Rates are a band, and Yuksom fills in October and April–May trekking weeks. Check current status before you travel.
why: Walk to Norbugang, Kathok Lake and the Dubdi trail
A comfortable bed before or after Goecha La
Terrace and garden in a quiet village

faqs.q: Is Yuksum Residency close to the Goecha La trailhead?
faqs.a: Yes. The trail into Khangchendzonga National Park starts at the top of Yuksom village, a short walk or drive from the hotel. Trekkers often spend the night before the trek here after finishing permits, and return for a hot shower when they come down. Ask us to hold luggage you do not need on the trail.

faqs.q: How far is Yuksom from Pelling?
faqs.a: About 40 km and 2 hours by car via the Rimbi and Kanchenjunga waterfalls. Many people visit Yuksom as a day trip from Pelling, but staying a night lets you see Norbugang, Kathok Lake and Dubdi without hurrying, and puts you in place for Tashiding the next morning, about 19 km away.

faqs.q: Is there mobile network and ATM in Yuksom?
faqs.a: Mobile data works in the village on the main networks, though it can be patchy and fails in long power cuts. There may be an ATM in the bazaar, but it is not reliable, so carry enough cash from Gangtok, Jorethang or Gyalshing for homestays, porters and small shops. Card and UPI acceptance varies.

name: Hotel Tashigang, Yuksom
summary: A long-running Yuksom hotel popular with trekkers and families, which can help arrange trekking equipment. A good-value, practical base for Norbugang, Dubdi and the start of the Goecha La trail.
body: Hotel Tashigang has been a fixture of Yuksom for many years and appears in most travel guides to the village. It is practical rather than fancy: clean rooms, hot water, a dining room and staff used to trekkers' early starts. The hotel can help arrange or point you to trekking equipment, which matters in a village where most trips into Khangchendzonga National Park begin.

We book it for value journeys and for trekkers who want a hotel rather than a homestay. From here Norbugang, Kathok Lake and the Dubdi trail are walkable. Rates are a band and rise in trekking season. Remember that trekking in Sikkim now needs a registered agency and a guide, so the hotel cannot sell you a solo permit. Check current status before you travel.
why: Practical base for trekkers and families
Help with trekking equipment
Walking distance to Yuksom's sights

faqs.q: Can Hotel Tashigang arrange a Goecha La trek?
faqs.a: The hotel can help with equipment and local advice, but the trek itself must go through a registered trekking agency with a licensed guide, who handles the Khangchendzonga National Park permit at Yuksom. We can arrange the trek with a registered local partner and book your nights at the hotel before and after. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does a room at Hotel Tashigang cost?
faqs.a: Indicatively ₹2,500–4,500 a room a night depending on room type and season, often with breakfast. It is busiest in October–November and April–May when trekking groups pass through. Winter and monsoon rates are lower. The ₹50 per person Sikkim tourist fee is collected at check-in.

faqs.q: Is Yuksom cold at night?
faqs.a: At about 1,780 m, Yuksom drops to around 3–6 °C on winter nights from December to February and stays mild, around 12–16 °C, on summer nights. Rooms are not centrally heated, so ask for an extra blanket or a heater in winter. Carry a fleece in every season, as evenings cool quickly after sunset.

name: Daragaon Village Retreat, Darap
price_band: ≈ ₹2,000–3,500 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: A community-minded eco homestay in Darap, the Limbu village 8 km from Pelling, offering farm walks, day hikes and home cooking. It won silver in the community homestay category of Outlook's Responsible Tourism Awards in 2017.
body: Darap is a mostly Limbu farming village about 8 km below Pelling at around 1,800 m, and Daragaon Village Retreat is its best-known homestay. Guests eat with the family, walk through cardamom, maize and vegetable fields, and take short hikes to viewpoints and the Rimbi river. The property received silver in Outlook Traveller's Responsible Tourism Awards in 2017 in the community-based homestay category.

We book it for travellers who want to see Limbu village life rather than a hotel corridor, and for families with children who like farms. Rooms are simple but comfortable. It is close enough to Pelling for sightseeing and on the road towards Yuksom and Khecheopalri. Rates are a band per person with meals. Check current status before you travel.
why: Home cooking and farm walks in a Limbu village
8 km from Pelling on the Yuksom road
Recognised for community-based tourism

faqs.q: What is there to do at Daragaon Village Retreat?
faqs.a: Farm and village walks, help in the fields or kitchen if you like, short hikes to viewpoints and the Rimbi river, and evenings talking with the family. The retreat can point you to Limbu cultural experiences in the village when they happen. Pelling's monasteries and Khecheopalri Lake are an easy day out by car.

faqs.q: How far is Darap from Pelling?
faqs.a: About 8 km, or 25–30 minutes by car, on the road that continues to Rimbi, Khecheopalri and Yuksom. A taxi from Pelling costs indicatively ₹500–800 one way. Staying in Darap gives you a quieter night than Pelling while keeping the Pelling sights within half an hour.

faqs.q: Is food at Darap homestays vegetarian?
faqs.a: Home cooking usually includes rice, dal, seasonal vegetables, local greens and pickles, with chicken or pork on many days. Vegetarian meals are easy to arrange if you say so when booking. Ask to try local dishes such as gundruk (fermented greens) and kinema (fermented soybean), which are common in Limbu kitchens.

name: Hotel Garuda, Pelling
summary: Pelling's long-standing backpacker favourite in Upper Pelling, near the helipad viewpoint, with good-value rooms, Kangchenjunga views from the terraces and a restaurant serving Sikkimese food.
body: Hotel Garuda is a budget classic in Upper Pelling, listed in guidebooks for years. Rooms are simple and fairly priced, the common terraces face Kangchenjunga, and the restaurant serves Sikkimese and Indian dishes. Staff help with shared jeep timings and sightseeing cars, which saves budget travellers a lot of asking around.

We use it for budget journeys and solo travellers. The helipad viewpoint, with one of the widest views in Pelling, is about 10 minutes' walk away. Upper rooms cost more and have better windows. Rates are a band and climb in October, late December and May. Check current status before you travel.
why: Budget rooms with terrace views of Kangchenjunga
Ten minutes' walk to the helipad viewpoint
Help with shared jeeps and sightseeing cars

faqs.q: Is Hotel Garuda in Upper Pelling?
faqs.a: Yes, it is in Upper Pelling near the main junction, where shared jeeps arrive and leave. The helipad viewpoint is about a 10-minute walk, and cafes and shops are close. Pemayangtse and Rabdentse are a short taxi ride away, and the Chenrezig statue and Skywalk about 15 minutes by car.

faqs.q: How do I get to Pelling on a budget?
faqs.a: Take a shared jeep from Gangtok or Siliguri to Gyalshing, indicatively ₹350–500 from Gangtok and ₹500–650 from Siliguri, then a shared or reserved local taxi for the last 10 km to Pelling. A few jeeps run direct to Pelling, mostly in the morning. Book the day before in peak season. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Garuda arrange sightseeing?
faqs.a: Staff can arrange local cars for the standard Pelling sightseeing loops, such as a half-day round of Pemayangtse, Rabdentse, the Skywalk and Sanga Choeling, or a full day to Khecheopalri, the waterfalls and Yuksom. Indicative rates are ₹2,500–3,500 for a half day and ₹3,500–5,000 for a full day per car.

name: Yuksom village homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,200–2,200 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: Family homestays around Yuksom, several linked to the Khangchendzonga Conservation Committee, a Yuksom-based community group. A low-cost, local way to stay at the gateway to Khangchendzonga National Park.
body: Yuksom has a cluster of family homestays in and around the village, from rooms above the bazaar to farmhouses on the slopes towards Dubdi. The Khangchendzonga Conservation Committee, a community group based in Yuksom, has long promoted homestays as a way for villagers to earn from tourism without building hotels. Expect a simple room, shared or attached bathroom, and home-cooked dal, rice, vegetables and local greens.

We place budget travellers and trekkers here and choose the family to suit the group. Hot water may come in a bucket, power cuts happen, and some homes are up steep paths, so pack light. The reward is time with a local family at the place where Sikkim's kingdom began. Check current status before you travel.
why: Low-cost stays with local families
Community-led tourism in a heritage village
Ideal before and after the Goecha La trek

faqs.q: What is the Khangchendzonga Conservation Committee?
faqs.a: It is a community organisation based in Yuksom that works on conservation and responsible tourism around Khangchendzonga National Park, including training trekking staff and promoting homestays. It is a useful contact for understanding local rules on waste and campsites. Its activities change over time, so ask us what it currently runs.

faqs.q: Are Yuksom homestays good for families?
faqs.a: Yes, for families comfortable with simple rooms. Children enjoy farm animals and the short walks to Norbugang and Kathok Lake. Some homes have attached bathrooms and some share one, so tell us what you need. The village is safe and quiet, and dinner with the family is often the highlight of the trip.

faqs.q: How much do Yuksom homestays cost?
faqs.a: Indicatively ₹1,200–2,200 per person a night including dinner and breakfast, sometimes all meals. Rooms with attached bathrooms cost more. Prices rise slightly in trekking weeks. Pay in cash where possible, as card and UPI acceptance varies. The ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee may be collected by the host.

name: Uttarey village homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,200–2,200 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: Family homestays in Uttarey, the cool village at about 2,000 m on the Singalila Ridge near the Nepal border, beyond the Singshore Bridge. Simple rooms, home cooking and forest walks for travellers who want quiet.
body: Uttarey sits at about 2,000 m on the northern slopes of the Singalila Ridge, about 35 km from Pelling, and has become a homestay village in the last two decades. Families with Limbu, Bhutia and Nepali roots host guests in simple rooms, cook with produce from their fields and point the way to the Mainebas waterfall, the Kagyu monastery and the forest road towards Chewabhanjang on the Nepal border.

We send travellers here who want a quiet night after the Singshore Bridge, or a base for gentle forest walks. Winters are cold, with snow on the ridge some years, and rooms are not heated, so ask for extra blankets. Uttarey is a long drive on a narrow road; leave Pelling by early afternoon. Check current status before you travel.
why: Cool, quiet village on the Singalila Ridge
Home cooking with local families
Close to the Singshore Bridge and forest walks

faqs.q: How far is Uttarey from Pelling?
faqs.a: About 35 km, or 1.5–2 hours by car, via Dentam and the Singshore Bridge. A reserved car from Pelling costs indicatively ₹2,500–3,500 one way. Shared jeeps run between Gyalshing and Uttarey a few times a day, mostly in the morning. Roads are narrow; avoid driving after dark.

faqs.q: Can foreigners cross into Nepal at Chewabhanjang from Uttarey?
faqs.a: No. Chewabhanjang is a border pass on the Singalila Ridge, about 10 km from Uttarey, and it is not an official crossing for foreign travellers. Indian and Nepali nationals have traditionally used local paths there, but rules change. We do not plan crossings; treat the trail as a forest walk and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Uttarey?
faqs.a: October to December for clear views and dry trails, and March to May for rhododendrons and green forests. January and February are cold and can bring snow on the ridge, which some travellers love. June to September is wet, with leeches on the trails and slides on the road, so we avoid it.
